lines: Nine sine LFOs, one for each planet of the solar system and Pluto, each cycling once per that planet's orbit, with a trigger at the end of every orbit and one knob that speeds them all up together
Speeds every LFO up together, from real time at fully counter-clockwise to an Earth year every millisecond at fully clockwise
Sets every phase back to zero while it is held down, and springs back when released; there is no way to put the phases back where they were
Anything above 0.1V here sets every phase back to zero, and holds them all at zero while it stays high
A 10V pulse each time Mercury finishes an orbit
A 10V pulse each time Venus finishes an orbit
A 10V pulse each time Earth finishes an orbit
A 10V pulse each time Mars finishes an orbit
A 10V pulse each time Jupiter finishes an orbit
A 10V pulse each time Saturn finishes an orbit
A 10V pulse each time Uranus finishes an orbit
A 10V pulse each time Neptune finishes an orbit
A 10V pulse each time Pluto finishes an orbit
A sine swinging 5V either way, one cycle per Mercury orbit of 88 Earth-days
A sine swinging 5V either way, one cycle per Venus orbit of 224.7 Earth-days
A sine swinging 5V either way, one cycle per Earth orbit of 365.2 days
A sine swinging 5V either way, one cycle per Mars orbit of 687 Earth-days
A sine swinging 5V either way, one cycle per Jupiter orbit of 4331 Earth-days
A sine swinging 5V either way, one cycle per Saturn orbit of 10747 Earth-days
A sine swinging 5V either way, one cycle per Uranus orbit of 30589 Earth-days
A sine swinging 5V either way, one cycle per Neptune orbit of 59800 Earth-days
A sine swinging 5V either way, one cycle per Pluto orbit of 90560 Earth-days
Note — no planet is named anywhere on the panel; which jack belongs to which planet is only in the hover text, and the pairs run outward in orbital order from Mercury
Note — the starting phases are worked out when the module is added to the patch, from how far through its orbit each planet would be if all nine had started together at the beginning of 1970
Note — every rate is half of what the knob says: the phases move on every other sample but are stepped as though every sample counted, so at the realtime setting an Earth cycle takes two years
Note — six lamps around the Speed knob light one at a time, where an Earth year is compressed into a year, a day, an hour, a minute, a second and a millisecond; between those settings none is lit
Note — the module is monophonic: every output carries one channel

PlanetaryLFOs.notes: Read at commit f845b65 (AFHawthorn/HawthornLabs), the tip of master. Seven commits carry 2.0.2. The installed manifest is byte-identical from e96f41c onward, which rules out the two earlier ones. Between the three that remain, the installed plugin.dylib settles it: the disassembly of PlanetaryLFOs::process holds two separate reads of the channels byte, one at Port+0x310 gating the sine write and one at Port+0x40 gating the trigger write, which is the split made in 84fbf87; the only later commit, f845b65, widens planetDur from long to long long, which changes nothing on arm64 where long is already 64-bit. The panel carries only four pieces of lettering - the title, Speed, reset and the brand - so none of the eighteen output jacks is named on it; the planet names exist only in configOutput. The word reset labels both the input jack and the button below it, so both lines say which. Every configInput and configOutput is called once with the matching enum. Widget order does follow enum order, but the two enum runs interleave on the panel: the nine trigger jacks are outputs 0 to 8 and the nine sine jacks outputs 9 to 17, and each planet's pair sits together, so reading down a column alternates between the two runs. Two things the maker's README does not say. The phase is advanced only on every other sample (line 84, counter % 2 == 0) while the increment at line 87 is computed for a full sample, so every LFO runs at half the stated rate and every trigger pulse lasts twice its nominal 10ms. And the README gives Earth's year as 365.25 days while the constants in the source give 365.2; the source figure is the one in the lines, and the other eight periods in the README agree exactly with the planetDur array. A PulseGenerator is only stepped while its own jack is patched (line 96), so a trigger output that has been left unpatched across a wrap emits the remainder of that pulse when a cable is put in. The six lamps are not ParamWidgets and cannot be clicked, so they get a Note rather than a line. The module has no menu of its own.
